en: Let's start with some theory though.
Deno is browser compatible,
and I put that between quotes because it
does not mean that you can take any Deno
program and run the same code in the
browser.
For one, this does not work because
Deno is able to use TypeScript, the browser
is not. And in addition, Deno of course
exposes certain features like working with
the file system,
which simply are not supported by the
browser.
But what it means is that where it makes
sense,
APIs that you find in the browser are also
made available in Deno.
For example,
setting a timer with setTimeout, or sending
an HTTP request with fetch, or listening to
the startup of the script basically with the
onload event.
These are all
all APIs
that are available in the browser. You could
set a timer with setTimeout in the browser.
You can send an HTTP request with fetch in
the browser. So this all works in the
browser and this all also works in Deno
scripts.
And that's important. They are available on
the global window object in Deno.
So even though, if you think about it, we
don't really have a window for our demo
script. It's not running in the browser
window at least.
Still, there is a global window object where
these core functionalities are exposed. And
again, the idea is to be as close to the
browser as possible
because that's another
probably minor flaw
that the creator of Node found in Node after
it was created, obviously,
that in Node, certain things are not
available that are available in the browser
and that would make sense in Node as well,
or if they are available, some things are
named differently. For example, there is no
window object in Node.
And he wanted to fix this for Deno so that
we basically don't have to learn a lot of
new things, or at least not as much, but
that we can reuse our knowledge which we
already have from the browser. And if we
wanna send an HTTP request, which you
sometimes wanna do in a server-side code
snippet as well, for example, you can just
use the Fetch API and you don't have to
learn about a new Deno-exclusive API for
doing that.
That's the idea of making it browser
compatible between quotes.
Now let's take a closer look at that and in
general,
let's take a closer look at the built-in
features Deno ships with.
